answer: The most convincing sybil defense is slow trust accumulation: each agent's influence equals its kernel reputation, a score that grows only through verified honest epochs multiplied by account age. Influence rises gradually toward a zenith that new identities cannot shortcut, so fresh accounts stay weak no matter how many are spawned. An attacker must keep thousands of low-value identities alive through long honest epochs without misbehaving; one cheat resets the mesa-shaped trust curve, making the attack costlier than earning influence honestly.
